title: Insurance Coverage & Claims: Amount Carried by a Corrected Claim for a Patient-Identification Denial
content:
**Insurance Coverage & Claims.** The amount a corrected claim carries when Halverson Clinical Laboratories answers a patient-identification denial (CO-31) on a claim held by a coverage is the denied amount being resubmitted.

## Clause

The claim corrected is the claim carrying the most recent patient-identification denial on the coverage, the order is the order that claim bills, and the order's invoice is the patient invoice that bills that order. The denial's amount is the claim's patient-identification denial amount; the claim's filing date and the amount it billed at filing are those of its original submission.

The amount the corrected claim carries is the identification correction's base, held to no more than the denial's amount, less the order's credits that come off; the amount carried is never below zero and is rounded half up to the cent once, at the end, with no rounding before the final cent. The identification correction's base is the denial's amount, and no order credit comes off: the corrected claim resubmits the denial's amount in full.

## Condition and result

| Element | Value |
|---|---|
| Base | The denial's amount |
| Ceiling on the base | The denial's amount |
| Order credits that come off | None |
| Floor | Zero |
| Rounding | Half up to the cent, once, at the end |

## Worked figures (hypothetical denials)

- A CO-31 denial of 212.35 USD: the corrected claim carries **212.35 USD**.
- Two CO-31 denial lines of 40.00 and 25.50 USD on the same claim: the denial's amount is 65.50 USD, and the corrected claim carries **65.50 USD**.
